title: In the non-bipartite case the set A of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition stays below the threshold throughout the window
author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the size bound for the set A of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition in the non-bipartite case (author lemma at source lines 1416-1419, label lem:nonbipartite-ge). Its proof (source lines 1420-1635) is the longest in the paper and is a probabilistic argument built on the decomposition: it fixes p in the window, assumes the deficiency is at least two and A larger than the threshold, and then combines the exact edge-counting identity for the Gallai-Edmonds parameters, the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph and the weighted counting bound for bipartitions of a set with a small boundary to force a contradiction. The chain is what makes the random part of the main theorem work in the non-bipartite case, and the author notes that the bipartite case needs separate treatment. H2.
